title: Component Instance Model
description: One configured use of a registered component within a page. Validation is two-level and cannot be otherwise: this schema checks structure, and the platform validator then checks the 'config' object against the properties schema of the manifest resolved from (type, typeVersion) at the page's pinned registry version. A static schema alone cannot express that, which is why the manifest is a runtime artifact rather than documentation.

typeVersion.description: Component contract version this instance was authored against. Pinning it is what stops a component change from silently altering a published page.

description.description: Accessible description and hover help. Populated by generation, since a generated widget must explain itself without a human writing help text.

config.description: Component-specific properties, validated against the manifest's properties schema. Closed there, so an invented property is a validation failure rather than a silently ignored field.

dataSource.description: Default data source for this instance's bindings. A binding may override it, which is how one component combines a value from one source with a comparison from another.

encodings.description: Chart encodings, for components whose dataRequirement shape is 'series'. Present instead of, not alongside, positional bindings.

slots.description: Child layout for layout and composite components, keyed by the slot names the manifest declares.

eventActions.description: Maps component events to page actions. The component emits 'rowActivated'; the page decides that means drill through to the security detail experience. This indirection is what keeps components context-free and interaction AI-generatable.

writesTo.description: Channels this component publishes to. Declared rather than inferred, so the renderer can build the invalidation graph at compile time and so the Studio can show an author what a widget affects.

stateOverrides.description: Overrides for the six mandated states. Present so a page can say something domain-specific — 'No exceptions outstanding' rather than 'No data' — without a component variant.

deniedBehaviour.description: What to render when the caller lacks entitlement to this component's data. Default 'deniedState' is deliberate: silently hiding a widget makes a page look complete when it is not, and 'not available to you' is honest and legible. Hiding is available where the widget's existence is itself sensitive.

notes.description: Author or generator commentary. Not rendered.

action.description: Recovery affordance — retry, clear filters, request access.
